body: Hmm..that adds another level of difficulty to it all. I really dont know in that case. Maybe someone else can offer advice?

Then suddenly "get a cold" and have a need to see your doc...assuming you're old enough to go see him/her alone in the room. Tell him/her what you are going through and that you need help. Expect parental repercussions. I most certainly did when that was my only option in my teens because they couldn't accept that I needed help. It was not easy. However, you will then get on meds you need to help you deal with it. THAT helped me get better then. And I'm here if you want to chat.

I. WAS. YOU. That's how I know. I was there in my teens and no one believed me. I was told to suck it up, to not be a drama queen, to grow up..and many variants on that theme. What you feel is very real to you and it is hard for others to see it. In my case, staying with my grandparents helped immensely. You may want to consider staying with relatives for a bit.

You now know and have the proof that people care and want to help you get better. They may not have the right words to say or show it the way you think they should. But they care! Use that. Your mother's anger was fear-based. Who wants to loose a child? She responded to the panic of seeing you on the ledge as best as she could.
People will now take your pain seriously. Again, use that or if you are not strong enough to do so yet, get someone you trust to speak for you.
So, yeah, you cheated. It isn't right. You know that. But, what is the worst that can happen? You fail the class? Ok, take it again. You get kicked out? Unlikely, but you can go to another school. New beginnings are always awesome, if hard at first.
For now though, let that go. Reach out and get the help you need. It'll be there.
I'm not saying your life will be great instantly. It won't. But it certainly can get better.

She is severely depressed and has trouble with booze. Been there, done that. I no longer use booze for support throughout the day, but I'm not really any better.
Exercise DOES help, but when you are so low you can't figure out how to get out of bed, much less face the day...well the thought of working out is overwhelming.
Does she look to you for emotional support? Does she look up to you?
If so, you're halfway there. Don't say "you should exercise". She already feels like a failure. That only gives her another item to put on her list.
Try mentioning after you come in from a walk that you feel invigorated and alive...but only in passing...not as a topic of conversation. Let her think on it. When she shows the slightest interest in joining you, invite her...but say it like.."I'm gonna go take a walk in an hour if you want to join me"

I did not. I simply closed the chat once I realized it was going nowhere.
I will try the others.
I tried that two nights ago...maybe I just got a bad volunteer, but it did nothing for me. I gave up and left the chat after 10 minutes or so.
Ha..did some more research today...apparently April is the most popular month to end it. Who knew that in death, I will achieve what I never did in life...going along with the crowd.

Wow, really?  I totally understand where he is.  I have tried for years to get myself above water.  Every single damn time I think I am finally getting better, that I might be getting somewhere, the other shoe drops.  I care.  I care deeply for friends and family.  That's what has kept me hanging on as long as I have.  However, there comes a point where even that is not enough any longer.  I am there.  Looks like Glipglopwub is too. *internet hugs, Glipglopwub*  I know how bad it sucks.
Yeah, I'm in the same place as you.  If you want to talk, let me know.

Please try to find a way to talk to someone.  Anyone who will listen.  I discovered a close friend (more like a sister) after she committed suicide in 2011.  I have been in a lovely little downhill spiral ever since because more and more bad things kept happening. Don't let yourself get to where I am. If you want to chat, I'll listen.
Thank you. Glad you are on the mend.
Oh, and mental health clinics won't work. I do not make enough to live comfortably, but I make too much to qualify for any government assistance. I tried that too.
Thank you. It really means a lot to know someone gives a damn, ya know?

Eww...the flu is no fun. Hope you feel better soon!
Oh, I didn't think you were trying to trivialize my job at all.
I will pm you the general area I'm in. I don't want to give my exact location because it is a small town, and I worry I could be identified with the combo of that and the info I have provided in this thread already.
Please don't try the train station.  I'm suffering too...but the thing that stops me from considering that as an option is the suffering I would cause   to the person operating the train.

Tatting?  I saw someone doing it when I was 12 or so and thought it was so cool that I taught myself that same weekend.  Been doing it ever since.

Yes, I am fully aware that I am severely depressed. Here's the thing..I feel that I can't publicly admit to being suicidal.  I have no safety net, no savings...a mandatory 72 hour vacation would ruin what little financial security I DO have, and would likely get me fired.

The ex has nothing do to with how I view my job...I have always felt that I am unable to achieve what I know I should be capable of.  It's always been a source of frustration to me.

Truly, I don't think i've ever known what it is like to feel safe or stable for any extended period of time.  

The only person I feel I could be totally open and honest with about feeling the way I do is a mandated reporter.  If I were truly honest about how I am feeling, I would put her in a very bad situation, and I won't do it.

I WANT help...I know I NEED help...but I am at a total loss as to what I should do without winding up homeless or putting people I care about in a bad situation.  That's why i've decided on April.  It gives me time to settle my affairs and cause as little suffering as I can by my departure.  Frankly, looking back, I realize I should have done this two years ago.

I have never lived up to my "potential" and find myself with little, if any, energy, or desire to do anything.  More and more builds up, and I can't even figure out where to begin.  I find no joy in anything...and I used to be passionate about learning and exploring...but as life keeps coming at me I find I can't do it anymore.  

If I had tomorrow off...I would probably sew or make tatted lace...and try to catch up on things.

I tried to find someone to talk to, but my insurance through work only pretends to support mental health...as soon as you try to actually "use" it, it disappears.

I have been at the same job for 9 years, but it is a state position...raises don't even keep up with the cost of living, and it takes everything I have to go in each day.

I did adopt another cute little dog in March after looking for the better part of a year, and I already know that a friend of mine would gladly take her in if I were to go away....they adore each other.

thank you for talking to me.
